title: Artificial Intelligence
overview: The cataloged AI major combines computing, mathematics, AI, ethics and cognitive psychology. Its represented core, named choices and course classifications have independent source reviews. Whole-degree certification remains partial because the current graduation and transfer pages differ on whether a summer semester may count toward residence.

requirements.title: Major and degree totals
requirements.summary: The major requires 20–21 courses and 67–69 credit hours, including at least 10 courses and 33 credit hours at level 300 or above. The degree requires at least 120 credit hours. Course choices determine the ranges.

requirements.title: Major GPA and transfer limits
requirements.summary: Major coursework requires a GPA of at least 2.00. After matriculation, at most five courses and 20 credit hours of transfer or study abroad credit may apply to specific major requirements; departmental equivalency approval is required.

requirements.title: Course substitutions
requirements.summary: Unlisted substitutions require the major advisor or applicable director of undergraduate studies to approve them and the official certifier to record them in Degree Works.

requirements.title: Catalog authority and applicable year
requirements.summary: The General Announcements govern over other Rice publications. Choose a documented GA year between matriculation and graduation; after more than seven years use last readmission through graduation. Departments may decline old coursework for program requirements after review, while it remains on the transcript. A newly created program is available from its appearance in the GA, not an inferred first teaching date.

requirements.title: University residency and minimum degree hours
requirements.summary: Complete the major and at least 120 semester hours, including 60 at Rice, 48 at level 300+, at least 25 of those upper-level hours at Rice and more than half of upper-level major work at Rice (or a stricter major rule). The graduation page permits one summer within four full-time residency semesters; the transfer page says four full fall/spring semesters. Preserve that conflict pending clarification.

requirements.title: Degree and major GPA, letter grades and standing
requirements.summary: Rice cumulative GPA must be at least 1.67, with at least 2.00 across Rice coursework satisfying each major/minor/certificate. Program courses need their earned letter grades: a needed P grade is uncovered on request or in the final audit and cannot be restored. Students must be in good academic/disciplinary standing and not under investigation. The major may impose higher standards.

requirements.title: LPAP and college-course credit caps
requirements.summary: No more than four LPAP hours or three student-taught COLL hours (including COLL 100–199 and COLL 200) count toward total graduation hours.

requirements.title: First-year writing and placement
requirements.summary: Complete and pass a three-credit FWIS in the first Rice year using letter grading. The prematriculation writing assessment determines placement; missing it defaults to FWIS 100. A student placed in FWIS 100 must pass that preparatory course in the first semester before the graduation FWIS; FWIS 100 itself does not meet the writing requirement.

requirements.title: Writing transfer and enrollment restrictions
requirements.summary: Freshman entrants cannot replace FWIS with prior transfer work. Transfer entrants must request a director-approved equivalent worth at least 2.5 semester hours in their first Rice semester. Neither group can take an external substitute after matriculation. During the first two weeks, a section change requires simultaneously adding another; later drops require an extraordinary committee exception.

requirements.title: Distribution groups and designation timing
requirements.summary: Complete three designated courses of at least three credit hours in each of Groups I, II and III; each group must span at least two departments, with divisional/interdisciplinary designations counting as departments. An approved transfer equivalent must carry at least 2.5 semester hours. Designation is determined at registration/taking, or matriculation for prior work. These are term-dependent eligibility rules, not a fixed invented course pool. Eligible major work may also satisfy distribution.

requirements.title: Analyzing Diversity and overlap
requirements.summary: Pass one AD-designated course of at least three credit hours. AD also carries distribution or FWIS eligibility and may overlap those requirements. An external equivalent needs approved AD designation when taken, or at matriculation for prior study. Completion in the first two years is encouraged, not a mandatory extra deadline.

requirements.title: Lifetime physical activity requirement
requirements.summary: Complete one one-credit LPAP course, with disability arrangements available. First-year completion is encouraged, including transfer students without an equivalent, not represented as an additional universal deadline.

requirements.title: Degree application and faculty conferral
requirements.summary: Apply for the degree by the published semester deadline; late application carries a fee. Faculty approval and completion of all applicable requirements precede December, May or August conferral. Ceremony participation is distinct from earning the degree.

requirements.title: Conditional dual-degree requirements
requirements.summary: Only if pursuing a second concurrent bachelor degree: choose a different degree type and discipline, obtain the additional declaration/advisor approval, complete both sets of requirements, and earn at least 30 additional Rice semester hours beyond the first degree. A second major alone is distinct and does not automatically constitute a second degree.

requirements.title: Transfer course and grade eligibility
requirements.summary: Transfer work needs recognized institutional accreditation and at least C- equivalent, with official transcripts. Pass/fail, noncollegiate/life-experience, equivalency exams such as CLEP, remedial/life-skills, MOOCs and fields not offered at Rice do not transfer. Previously passed Rice courses do not earn duplicate transfer credit unless repeatable or exceptionally approved by the dean/vice provost.

requirements.title: Transfer limits, GPA and converted hours
requirements.summary: Postmatriculation summer transfer is capped at 15 semester hours except official summer study abroad. Concurrent external work remains subject to course-load rules and stricter program limits. Transfer normally has no Rice GPA effect; an explicitly approved curricular component can instead carry all grades, including below C-. Registrar-determined semester-hour/level conversion applies; ECTS has an explicit 0.5 semester-hour relation, not a generic conversion for other systems.

requirements.title: Equivalent credit versus general transfer electives
requirements.summary: Seek approval before external study. Without departmental equivalent-course approval, eligible work normally receives upper- or lower-level TRAN elective credit. Reclassification to a Rice equivalent reduces TRAN by the same hours, avoiding duplicate credit. The registrar evaluates only after receipt of an official transcript.

requirements.title: International transfer evaluation and study-abroad exceptions
requirements.summary: Foreign work needs a professional course-by-course equivalency/grade/level evaluation. Official Rice study abroad is normally exempt unless the registrar cannot determine credit clearly. Third-party study abroad needs a School of Record transcript; direct-enrollment study may still need evaluation when credit is unclear.

requirements.title: Course load and outside-registration approvals
requirements.summary: For the AI degree, registration above 18 semester hours including concurrent external coursework needs prior written overload approval; below 12 hours in fall/spring needs reduced-load permission. Completing degree requirements elsewhere or concurrent enrollment also needs the specified advance written approval. An external course is not recorded without prior concurrent-enrollment authorization.

requirements.title: Full-time enrollment and graduate-course permission
requirements.summary: Undergraduate full-time status requires 12 semester hours, including summer. Courses 100–299 are lower-level and 300–499 upper-level. Enrolling outside the undergraduate level needs an instructor-permission override; an elective listing does not independently waive enrollment requirements.

requirements.title: Repeat, prior-credit and cross-list accounting
requirements.summary: All attempts and grades remain on the transcript and in GPA. Repeating a passed nonrepeatable course earns credit only once, for the highest grade; repeating prior AP/transfer work removes that prior credit. Explicitly repeatable courses follow their designation. Cross-listed, equivalent and undergraduate/graduate equivalent courses cannot earn duplicate credit, concurrently or across terms unless repeatable.

requirements.title: AI senior design sequencing
requirements.summary: COMP 456 and COMP 457 must be completed in sequence within the same academic year. This timing condition does not add another course to the two fixed senior-design requirements.

requirements.title: Published vision elective registration condition
requirements.summary: COMP 345 and COMP 447 contain reciprocal registration exclusions based on prior credit. The registrar explicitly permits an instructor-approved mutual-exclusion registration override. This is a conditional approval route, not a contradictory degree requirement or guaranteed permission. No separate duplicate-credit prohibition is inferred from this registration wording.

requirements.title: Graduate-only elective restrictions
requirements.summary: COMP585 and631 list Graduate-level enrollment restrictions. The GA and registrar provide an instructor-approved level-override route; the undergraduate elective listing is not itself permission.

requirements.title: Conditional statistics preparation
requirements.summary: COMP345/346 require STAT315, and STAT314 requires STAT310 (concurrent permitted). The published STAT310+314 or STAT311+314 degree routes can therefore require instructor-approved prerequisite exceptions for later enrollment. STAT315 and the alternative statistics courses also carry prior-credit registration exclusions, for which the registrar provides a conditional override route. No automatic equivalence, granted waiver, extra universal fixed course or duplicate-credit entitlement is inferred.

requirements.title: Mutually Exclusive conditional registration route
requirements.summary: Mutual-exclusion registration errors may be overridden only with instructor/department approval through an electronic Course Registration Override in ESTHER. The ordinary exclusion remains in force without approval. This is a conditional registration route, not guaranteed approval or an independent declaration of duplicate degree-credit entitlement.

requirements.title: Prerequisite and Test Score conditional registration route
requirements.summary: A missing prerequisite must be completed or an instructor-permission Course Registration Override obtained through ESTHER. Thus the published alternative statistics routes can require approved exceptions for entry to later courses; no extra course, automatic waiver or guaranteed approval is inferred.

requirements.title: Instructor-approved registration exceptions
requirements.summary: Request the needed prerequisite or level exception electronically through ESTHER. Instructor approval and subsequent completion of registration are distinct steps; a submitted request is not permission. Individual decisions are not inferred from a published degree option.

notes: Major requirements are observed from the catalog; sample plans and optional graduate opportunities are not degree requirements.

University degree rules are mapped from the 2026–2027 General Announcements: residence/credit/GPA/standing, FWIS and transfer limits, three distribution groups, Analyzing Diversity, LPAP, catalog-year selection and degree application. Term-dependent designation criteria remain rules rather than invented fixed pools.

The graduation and transfer pages disagree on summer eligibility for the four-semester residency minimum. Both are GA pages; the GA precedence statement does not resolve this internal conflict. Curriculum remains partial pending clarification.

Transfer and registration rules preserve C- eligibility, no pass/fail transfers, the summer transfer cap and study-abroad exception, external-study approvals, repeat/AP/transfer/cross-list accounting and instructor approval for graduate-level enrollment.

2026-10-11 independent core correctness pass: official descriptions correct all13 fixed subject classifications (3 foundations,1 mathematics,5 AI/ML,2 systems,1 human context,1 applications). Exact ARTIFICAL source spellings are preserved. Capstone456/457 must be sequential in the same academic year. Course-entry conditions remain explicit; the subsequent registrar-policy review resolves their exception mechanism.

All43 degree-listed course identities and individual credit amounts were reviewed against exact2026–2027 department descriptions. Source-listed aliases remain separate option records but cross-list rules prohibit duplicate credit. Individual credit units are semester_hours, corroborated by the university registration policy, without conversion.

COMP631 and COMP462 retain explicit mixed reviews rather than an unsupported single subject. PSYC468 is human_context, COMP414 mathematics, and COMP409/480/585 computing foundations based on their actual descriptions.

Three independently reviewed reciprocal cross-list groups preserve43 source records but yield39 mapped course identities:13 fixed and26 options. Statistics315/DSCI301, vision447 and the three robotics450 aliases are deduplicated only through explicit source evidence; selection quantities remain unchanged.

Registrar policy explicitly permits instructor-approved mutual-exclusion and prerequisite overrides. COMP345/447 registration restrictions and the alternative statistics routes are therefore conditional approval paths, not unresolved curriculum contradictions. Individual permission and duplicate-credit entitlement are not presumed. The GA residency wording disagreement remains the only unresolved requirement interpretation.
